title: IELTS Academic Mock Test 4
description: Listening module for IELTS Academic Mock Test 4 with a single continuous audio file and 40 questions.

modules.instructions: Listen to the full recording and answer the questions for each part.

sections.title: Listening Part 1: Roommate Issues
sections.instructions: Questions 1-6: Complete the table below. Write ONE WORD ONLY for each answer. Questions 7-10: Complete the notes. Write NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS for each answer.

questions.question_instructions: Write ONE WORD ONLY.
questions.question_text: Behavior: Positive Points - He is ___
questions.passage_excerpt: On the plus side regarding his behavior, he is usually completely silent around the house.
questions.what_question_asks: A positive trait regarding his behavior.
questions.what_passage_says: He is very quiet and silent.
questions.tip: Listen for positive adjectives related to behavior.
questions.explanation: The speaker mentions 'silent' as a positive aspect of his behavior.

questions.question_instructions: Write ONE WORD ONLY.
questions.question_text: Behavior: Negative Points - He is ___
questions.passage_excerpt: However, the downside is that he can often be quite rude when you try to talk to him.
questions.what_question_asks: A negative trait regarding his behavior.
questions.what_passage_says: He often acts rude.
questions.tip: Contrasting linkers like 'however' introduce the negative points.
questions.explanation: The speaker uses 'rude' to describe the negative side of his behavior.

questions.question_instructions: Write ONE WORD ONLY.
questions.question_text: His Friends: Positive Points - His friends visit ___
questions.passage_excerpt: It's good that his friends visit rarely, so the house doesn't get crowded.
questions.what_question_asks: Frequency of his friends visiting.
questions.what_passage_says: His friends do not visit often.
questions.why_answer: 'Rarely' fits the grammatical constraint and meaning.
questions.tip: Adverbs of frequency are common answers in Part 1.
questions.explanation: The speaker appreciates that visits from friends happen 'rarely'.

questions.question_instructions: Write ONE WORD ONLY.
questions.question_text: His Friends: Negative Points - They ___
questions.passage_excerpt: The problem with his friends, though, is that they smoke inside.
questions.what_question_asks: A negative action his friends do.
questions.what_passage_says: They have a habit of smoking indoors.
questions.why_answer: 'Smoke' is the verb describing their negative action.
questions.tip: Listen for negative habits.
questions.explanation: The speaker explicitly states that his friends 'smoke'.

questions.question_instructions: Write ONE WORD ONLY.
questions.question_text: Other: Positive Points - He pays rent ___
questions.passage_excerpt: One great thing is that whenever rent is due, he pays it instantly.
questions.what_question_asks: How or when he pays rent.
questions.what_passage_says: He pays his rent immediately.
questions.why_answer: 'Instantly' describes the promptness of his rent payment.
questions.tip: Look for adverbs describing the verb 'pays'.
questions.explanation: The transcript confirms he pays rent 'instantly'.

questions.question_instructions: Write ONE WORD ONLY.
questions.question_text: Other: Negative Points - He doesn't ___ with others
questions.passage_excerpt: But on the other hand, he doesn't comply with the rules we set with others.
questions.what_question_asks: An action he fails to do with others.
questions.what_passage_says: He refuses to follow rules with other people.
questions.tip: The preposition 'with' is a strong clue for the verb 'comply'.
questions.explanation: The speaker mentions he doesn't 'comply' with others.

questions.question_instructions: Write NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS.
questions.question_text: Issues to Discuss: Communication: ___
questions.passage_excerpt: For communication, we need to insist that he join meetings to stay updated.
questions.what_question_asks: What needs to be discussed regarding communication.
questions.what_passage_says: He needs to participate in meetings.
questions.why_answer: 'Join meetings' is the exact two-word action required.
questions.tip: Note the word limit allows for up to two words.
questions.explanation: The note requires the action 'join meetings' for communication.

questions.question_instructions: Write NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS.
questions.question_text: Issues to Discuss: Friends: ___
questions.passage_excerpt: Regarding his friends, we must tell them to respect rules when they visit.
questions.what_question_asks: What must be discussed about his friends.
questions.what_passage_says: Friends need to follow the house rules.
questions.tip: Listen for imperatives or strong suggestions.
questions.explanation: The required discussion point is that friends must 'respect rules'.

questions.question_instructions: Write NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS.
questions.question_text: Issues to Discuss: Cigarettes: ___
questions.passage_excerpt: We should make it clear that cigarettes are strictly banned inside the property.
questions.what_question_asks: The policy on cigarettes.
questions.what_passage_says: Cigarettes are completely prohibited.
questions.why_answer: The phrase 'strictly banned' describes the rule on cigarettes.
questions.tip: Adverb + adjective combinations are common in notes completion.
questions.explanation: The transcript explicitly states cigarettes are 'strictly banned'.

questions.question_instructions: Write NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS.
questions.question_text: Issues to Discuss: Cleaning: must ___
questions.passage_excerpt: Finally, we need to agree that cleaning must be done every weekend.
questions.what_question_asks: What must happen regarding cleaning.
questions.what_passage_says: Cleaning has to be completed.
questions.tip: Check that your answer grammatically follows 'must'.
questions.explanation: The speaker notes that cleaning must 'be done'.

sections.title: Listening Part 2: Seminar Event Details
sections.instructions: Questions 11-16: Complete the sentences below. Write ONE WORD ONLY for each answer. Questions 17-20: Complete the notes below. Write ONE WORD AND/OR A NUMBER for each answer.

questions.question_instructions: Write ONE WORD ONLY.
questions.question_text: Before the seminar begins, the speaker will explain the ___ for the event.
questions.passage_excerpt: Just before we kick off the seminar, I will run through the schedule for the entire event.
questions.what_question_asks: What the speaker will explain before the event.
questions.what_passage_says: The speaker will explain the itinerary/schedule.
questions.why_answer: 'Schedule' is the single word matching what will be explained.
questions.tip: Listen for synonyms of 'explain'.
questions.explanation: The speaker says they will explain the 'schedule' before beginning.

questions.question_instructions: Write ONE WORD ONLY.
questions.question_text: Extra time has been included for ___ after every talk.
questions.passage_excerpt: You'll notice we've factored in some extra time for discussion following each of the talks.
questions.what_question_asks: What the extra time is allocated for.
questions.what_passage_says: Time is given for people to discuss.
questions.why_answer: The extra time is specifically for 'discussion'.
questions.tip: Distractors might include 'questions', but 'discussion' is explicitly stated.
questions.explanation: The transcript mentions extra time for 'discussion'.

questions.question_instructions: Write ONE WORD ONLY.
questions.question_text: Morning refreshments will be available at 11:30 in the ___ lounge.
questions.passage_excerpt: At 11:30, morning refreshments will be served over in the reading lounge.
questions.what_question_asks: The name of the lounge where refreshments are served.
questions.what_passage_says: Refreshments are in the reading lounge.
questions.why_answer: 'Reading' is the modifier for the lounge.
questions.tip: Proper nouns or specific descriptors for rooms are common answers.
questions.explanation: The lounge is specifically identified as the 'reading' lounge.

questions.question_instructions: Write ONE WORD ONLY.
questions.question_text: Lunch will be served in the bistro, and all attendees must bring their seminar ___.
questions.passage_excerpt: When heading to the bistro for lunch, please ensure you bring your seminar badge with you to gain entry.
questions.what_question_asks: What attendees must bring to lunch.
questions.what_passage_says: They need their badge for lunch.
questions.tip: Listen for obligatory phrases like 'must' or 'ensure you'.
questions.explanation: Attendees are required to bring their 'badge'.

questions.question_instructions: Write ONE WORD ONLY.
questions.question_text: The afternoon break is planned for the ___, if the weather allows.
questions.passage_excerpt: Assuming it doesn't rain, the afternoon break is scheduled to take place out on the terrace.
questions.what_question_asks: The location for the afternoon break, weather permitting.
questions.what_passage_says: The break will be on the terrace if it doesn't rain.
questions.paraphrase: if the weather allows = assuming it doesn't rain
questions.tip: Conditional phrases in the question often correspond to conditionals in the audio.
questions.explanation: The 'terrace' is the planned location, dependent on weather.

questions.question_instructions: Write ONE WORD ONLY.
questions.question_text: The organising ___ will gather in the heritage lounge after the final session.
questions.passage_excerpt: Once the final session wraps up, I'd like the organising committee to meet me in the heritage lounge.
questions.what_question_asks: Who will gather in the heritage lounge.
questions.what_passage_says: The committee needs to meet there.
questions.tip: Listen for collective nouns like team, group, or committee.
questions.explanation: The 'committee' is instructed to gather in the lounge.

questions.question_instructions: Write ONE WORD AND/OR A NUMBER.
questions.question_text: Schedule for Tomorrow: Break for lunch is planned at ___.
questions.passage_excerpt: Looking at tomorrow, our lunch break is slightly later, planned for exactly 1:15.
questions.what_question_asks: The specific time for the lunch break.
questions.what_passage_says: Lunch is at 1:15.
questions.tip: Times and dates are common targets for numbers.
questions.explanation: The speaker confirms lunch will be at '1:15'.

questions.question_instructions: Write ONE WORD AND/OR A NUMBER.
questions.question_text: Closing talk by Dr. Harrison will be held in the ___ Room.
questions.passage_excerpt: Dr. Harrison's closing talk has been moved, and it will now be in the Conference Room.
questions.what_question_asks: The specific room for the closing talk.
questions.what_passage_says: The talk is in the Conference Room.
questions.paraphrase: held in = will now be in
questions.tip: Watch out for last-minute room changes in the audio.
questions.explanation: The room assigned for the talk is the 'Conference' Room.

questions.question_instructions: Write ONE WORD AND/OR A NUMBER.
questions.question_text: Guests must go to the ___ desk to book a time for the steam room.
questions.passage_excerpt: If you wish to use the steam room, you need to head over to the front desk to reserve a slot.
questions.what_question_asks: Which desk guests must go to.
questions.what_passage_says: Guests must go to the front desk.
questions.paraphrase: reserve a slot = book a time
questions.tip: Adjectives modifying 'desk' are typical answers.
questions.explanation: The speaker directs guests to the 'front' desk.

questions.question_instructions: Write ONE WORD AND/OR A NUMBER.
questions.question_text: To use the steam room, a refundable ___ of £15 is required at reception.
questions.passage_excerpt: Please note that a refundable deposit of £15 will be asked for at reception for steam room access.
questions.what_question_asks: What the £15 payment represents.
questions.what_passage_says: The £15 is a deposit.
questions.paraphrase: is required = will be asked for
questions.tip: Listen for financial terms linked to amounts (e.g., fee, deposit, charge).
questions.explanation: The £15 is clearly stated to be a 'deposit'.

sections.title: Listening Part 3: Art Project Discussion
sections.instructions: Questions 21-25: Choose the correct letter, A, B, or C. Questions 26-30: Complete the sentences below. Write NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS for each answer.

questions.question_instructions: Choose the correct letter, A, B, or C.
questions.question_text: Why did Liam reject the idea of wood carving?
questions.passage_excerpt: I thought about wood carving at first, but honestly, it just feels a bit too ordinary and overdone for a final project.
questions.what_question_asks: The reason Liam decided against wood carving.
questions.what_passage_says: He felt wood carving was too common or ordinary.
questions.why_answer: Option B is correct as 'ordinary' directly matches his feeling that it's overdone.
questions.tip: Speakers often list distractors (time/expense) before giving their true reason.
questions.explanation: Liam rejected the idea because it felt 'ordinary'.

questions.question_instructions: Choose the correct letter, A, B, or C.
questions.question_text: What alternative approach does Liam suggest?
questions.passage_excerpt: Instead of sticking to one thing, I think combining different materials like glass and steel would be much more impactful.
questions.what_question_asks: Liam's suggested alternative method.
questions.what_passage_says: He suggests using multiple different materials together.
questions.paraphrase: combining different materials = using multiple materials together
questions.tip: Listen for phrases like 'Instead of' to signal the correct alternative.
questions.explanation: Liam specifically mentions 'combining different materials' as his preferred approach.

questions.question_instructions: Choose the correct letter, A, B, or C.
questions.question_text: What does Maya say about Professor Kane’s preferences?
questions.passage_excerpt: Professor Kane isn't strictly against modernism, but what he really values and prefers are strong cultural connections in the artwork.
questions.what_question_asks: Maya's insight on Professor Kane's preferences.
questions.what_passage_says: He values cultural connections.
questions.why_answer: Option C matches her statement about him preferring cultural connections.
questions.tip: Pay attention to words indicating preference like 'values most' or 'prefers'.
questions.explanation: Maya points out that Professor Kane values 'cultural connections'.

questions.question_instructions: Choose the correct letter, A, B, or C.
questions.question_text: Why does Maya suggest making a medium-sized sculpture?

options.option_text: Larger ones are hard to move

questions.passage_excerpt: I'd suggest sticking to a medium size, simply because the larger ones are incredibly hard to move around the studio.
questions.what_question_asks: The reason for Maya's size suggestion.
questions.what_passage_says: Large sculptures are difficult to transport/move.
questions.why_answer: Option A accurately reflects the difficulty in moving larger sculptures.
questions.paraphrase: hard to move = difficult to transport
questions.tip: The reason provided immediately after the suggestion is usually the correct answer.
questions.explanation: Maya explicitly states that larger ones are 'hard to move'.

questions.question_instructions: Choose the correct letter, A, B, or C.
questions.question_text: What production method do the students agree on?
questions.passage_excerpt: Let's not limit ourselves to just carving or just casting; a combination of both techniques makes the most sense.
questions.what_question_asks: The method they mutually agree to use.
questions.what_passage_says: They decide to combine carving and casting.
questions.why_answer: Option C is correct because they agree on 'a combination'.
questions.tip: In agreement questions, wait for both speakers to reach a consensus.
questions.explanation: They conclude that a 'combination' of methods is the best approach.

questions.question_instructions: Write NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS.
questions.question_text: Liam admits he needs to improve his ___.
questions.passage_excerpt: To be honest, the one thing I really need to improve is my patience when working on detailed parts.
questions.what_question_asks: What Liam feels he lacks or needs to improve.
questions.what_passage_says: Liam needs more patience.
questions.why_answer: 'Patience' is what he admits needing to improve.
questions.tip: Listen for self-reflective statements.
questions.explanation: Liam admits his 'patience' needs improvement.

questions.question_instructions: Write NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS.
questions.question_text: Maya struggles with achieving ___ in her sculptures.
questions.passage_excerpt: For me, the main struggle is always achieving clarity in the overall message of the sculpture.
questions.what_question_asks: What Maya finds difficult.
questions.what_passage_says: Maya has a hard time achieving clarity.
questions.why_answer: 'Clarity' is the attribute she struggles with.
questions.tip: Identify the core noun that follows 'achieving'.
questions.explanation: Maya states her struggle is achieving 'clarity'.

questions.question_instructions: Write NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS.
questions.question_text: The ___ will not be available until mid-March.
questions.passage_excerpt: We have to plan our timeline carefully because the foundry won't be available to us until mid-March.
questions.what_question_asks: What facility or item is unavailable until mid-March.
questions.what_passage_says: The foundry is booked until mid-March.
questions.why_answer: The 'foundry' is the specific place that is unavailable.
questions.paraphrase: not be available = won't be available
questions.tip: Listen for dates or timeframes as anchors.
questions.explanation: The speaker mentions the 'foundry' will be unavailable.

questions.question_instructions: Write NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS.
questions.question_text: Liam chose the seminar on art ___.
questions.passage_excerpt: I eventually decided to choose the seminar focused on art conservation.
questions.what_question_asks: The topic of Liam's chosen seminar.
questions.what_passage_says: Liam picked the conservation seminar.
questions.tip: Seminar topics are usually nouns or noun phrases.
questions.explanation: Liam selected the seminar on 'conservation'.

questions.question_instructions: Write NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS.
questions.question_text: Maya registered for the workshop on designing ___.
questions.passage_excerpt: And I just registered for that interesting workshop on designing an exhibition.
questions.what_question_asks: What Maya's workshop is about designing.
questions.what_passage_says: The workshop is about designing an exhibition.
questions.tip: Listen for 'designing' to find the subsequent noun.
questions.explanation: Maya registered to learn about designing an 'exhibition'.

sections.title: Listening Part 4: Mass Strandings of Whales and Dolphins
sections.instructions: Questions 31-40: Complete the notes below. Write NO MORE THAN THREE WORDS for each answer.

questions.question_instructions: Write NO MORE THAN THREE WORDS.
questions.question_text: Common in regions with ___
questions.passage_excerpt: These mass strandings are particularly common in regions characterized by complex coastlines.
questions.what_question_asks: The type of geographical feature where strandings are common.
questions.what_passage_says: They happen often near complex coastlines.
questions.paraphrase: common in regions with = common in regions characterized by
questions.tip: Adjective + noun combinations are frequent in Part 4.
questions.explanation: The transcript identifies 'complex coastlines' as the common regions.

questions.question_instructions: Write NO MORE THAN THREE WORDS.
questions.question_text: Sudden ___ can confuse animals unfamiliar with shallow waters.
questions.passage_excerpt: Animals can easily become disoriented when sudden tidal changes occur in shallow waters.
questions.what_question_asks: What sudden event confuses the animals.
questions.what_passage_says: Sudden changes in the tide confuse them.
questions.tip: Listen for synonyms of 'confuse', such as 'disorient' or 'baffle'.
questions.explanation: The audio explains that 'tidal changes' lead to confusion.

questions.question_instructions: Write NO MORE THAN THREE WORDS.
questions.question_text: Animals may panic when traveling in ___
questions.passage_excerpt: Panic can spread rapidly, especially when they are traveling in large social groups.
questions.what_question_asks: The formation or condition in which animals panic.
questions.what_passage_says: Panic spreads when they travel in big groups.
questions.tip: Three-word answers often include two adjectives and a noun.
questions.explanation: The animals panic particularly when in 'large social groups'.

questions.question_instructions: Write NO MORE THAN THREE WORDS.
questions.question_text: Parasites: Many stranded animals suffer from ___
questions.passage_excerpt: Upon examination, biologists found that many stranded animals suffer from severe parasitic infections.
questions.what_question_asks: What medical issue the animals suffer from.
questions.what_passage_says: They suffer from parasitic infections.
questions.why_answer: The phrase 'parasitic infections' is explicitly mentioned.
questions.tip: The heading 'Parasites' helps anticipate the noun 'infections'.
questions.explanation: The animals are found to suffer from 'parasitic infections'.

questions.question_instructions: Write NO MORE THAN THREE WORDS.
questions.question_text: Parasitic worms are often found in ___
questions.passage_excerpt: These parasitic worms are most frequently located in the inner ear regions of the mammals.
questions.what_question_asks: Where the worms are located in the body.
questions.what_passage_says: The worms are in the inner ear regions.
questions.paraphrase: often found in = most frequently located in
questions.tip: Anatomical terms are common in biology-related Part 4 passages.
questions.explanation: The worms are found in the 'inner ear regions'.

questions.question_instructions: Write NO MORE THAN THREE WORDS.
questions.question_text: Damage to ___ system can cause navigational errors.
questions.passage_excerpt: Any significant damage to their hearing system can directly result in fatal navigational errors.
questions.what_question_asks: Which system, when damaged, causes errors.
questions.what_passage_says: Damage to the hearing system causes navigation issues.
questions.why_answer: The blank requires the word 'hearing' to modify 'system'.
questions.tip: Context clues from the previous question ('ear') support 'hearing'.
questions.explanation: Navigational errors occur due to damage to the 'hearing' system.

questions.question_instructions: Write NO MORE THAN THREE WORDS.
questions.question_text: Toxins: Toxins can be derived from ___ or other sea creatures.
questions.passage_excerpt: Sometimes the cause is toxins, which can be derived from harmful algae or other smaller sea creatures.
questions.what_question_asks: A source of toxins besides sea creatures.
questions.what_passage_says: Toxins come from algae.
questions.why_answer: The word 'algae' is the specific source mentioned.
questions.tip: Listen for lists joined by 'or' / 'and'.
questions.explanation: The text lists 'algae' as a source of toxins.

questions.question_instructions: Write NO MORE THAN THREE WORDS.
questions.question_text: Affect the ___ system, causing confusion or weakness.
questions.passage_excerpt: These toxins severely affect the nervous system, leading to widespread confusion and muscle weakness.
questions.what_question_asks: Which bodily system is affected by toxins.
questions.what_passage_says: Toxins affect the nervous system.
questions.tip: Another anatomical/biological system term.
questions.explanation: The toxins are said to affect the 'nervous' system.

questions.question_instructions: Write NO MORE THAN THREE WORDS.
questions.question_text: Environmental Changes: Variations in ___, unusual currents, or magnetic fields can interfere with navigation
questions.passage_excerpt: Environmental factors play a role too; sudden variations in water temperature, along with unusual currents, disrupt their navigation.
questions.what_question_asks: An environmental variation that interferes with navigation.
questions.what_passage_says: Changes in water temperature affect navigation.
questions.why_answer: The specific variation mentioned is 'water temperature'.
questions.tip: Listen for environmental terminology.
questions.explanation: Variations in 'water temperature' are cited as a cause of interference.

questions.question_instructions: Write NO MORE THAN THREE WORDS.
questions.question_text: Human Activity: Marine mammals may be disturbed by ___ from shipping or offshore exploration.
questions.passage_excerpt: Finally, marine mammals are increasingly disturbed by intense underwater noise generated by commercial shipping and offshore exploration.
questions.what_question_asks: What human-generated disturbance affects marine mammals.
questions.what_passage_says: They are bothered by noise underwater from ships.
questions.tip: Look for the source of the disturbance mentioned in conjunction with shipping.
questions.explanation: The mammals are disturbed by 'underwater noise' from human activities.
